description: Web-tier coverage baseline (P1-27-QA-001). Scope is the `coverage.include` allow-list in apps/web/vitest.config.ts — the P1-27 CRM and Vehicle features, the dashboard routes that mount them, and the shared library under src/lib. Measured by `npm run test:web -- --coverage`, which runs BOTH vitest projects (`logic` in node, `dom` in jsdom) into one v8 report, because they are two environments over one application. Merging this with the unit or backend tier would overstate all three: those measure apps/api.
establishedBy: RE-ESTABLISHED at the vitest 4 upgrade. GitHub-hosted run id 34321869051, job `Web quality / web-quality`, artifact `evidence-web-quality`, file `apps/web/coverage/web/coverage-summary.json`, at branch head 64b8cb08b9f81be02ee627bcde83286c0bc25331, ubuntu-latest. 131 instrumented source files. ORIGINAL ESTABLISHMENT, kept for traceability: a LOCAL measurement in the p1-27/core-api-boundary worktree at base 0650a506b5990a809a3f350370b16e25edb1e7fd, `npm run test --workspace @rootlco/web -- --coverage`, 1533 tests across 70 test files, 0 failed, 90 instrumented source files — taken when this tier had NEVER been measured, because apps/web/vitest.config.ts declared two projects and no `coverage` block at all, the repository-root config's `include` list is entirely apps/api/src, and neither committed coverage baseline mentioned apps/web. The instrumented file count moved 90 -> 131 through ordinary growth of the four include roots between P1-27 and now, NOT through a change to the include list, which is byte-identical and pinned by apps/web/tests/security.test.ts.
reEstablishmentReason: @vitest/coverage-v8 moved from 3.2.7 to 4.1.11 (forced: the 3.x line carries no patched release for GHSA-82fw-gwwq-j7x9). Vitest 4 replaced the v8 provider's RANGE mapping with AST-aware remapping, so covered/total is computed over a different unit of account and the old figures are not comparable with the new ones. The branch that moved them changes NO application source. The clearest single signal is the `lines === statements` identity — byte-identical in every vitest-3 measurement of every tier in this repository, which is the range-mapping signature — DISAPPEARING at the major: this tier now reports 1875/2246 lines against 2064/2517 statements. See docs/engineering/ci-automation/coverage-policy.md, `When the coverage provider changes major version`.

previousBaselineBeforeReEstablishment.why: Kept so the re-establishment is a visible diff rather than a silent overwrite. Branches falls hardest (85.50 -> 77.37) and lines and statements RISE. Neither movement is a change in how well this tier is tested; both are the same code counted differently.

ciWiring: WIRED. The apps/web `test:ci` script carries the coverage flags, so the suite is executed once for both purposes, and `_reusable-node-quality.yml` runs `coverage-gate.mjs` against this baseline in the web-quality task. The flags live inside the workspace script deliberately: `npm run test:web -- --coverage` loses the separator at the second npm layer and runs a plain `vitest run`, which exits 0, writes no report, and produces a coverage job that measured nothing while calling itself a coverage run.
ciWiringTrap: DO NOT write step (1) as `npm run test:web -- --coverage`. Measured on this tree: npm appends the argument to the delegating script WITHOUT the `--` separator, so the line that actually executes is `npm run test --workspace @rootlco/web --coverage`, the inner npm swallows `--coverage` as one of its own config flags, and the command that runs is a bare `vitest run`. The suite passes, the job exits 0, no coverage report is emitted and no coverage directory is created — a green coverage job that measured nothing. The workspace-direct spelling above carries the flag through and is what every figure in this document was measured with. `npm run test:web` is still the registered command the reachability gate sees, because `check-command-coverage.mjs` follows the `--workspace` edge.
runtimeNote: Instrumentation slows the `dom` project materially, and that observation still stands. The figures it was written against do not: it described four coverage runs of the 70-file establishment tree reporting 1505/1505, and cited a `getByRole` timeout at `apps/web/tests/record-form-consumers.dom.test.tsx:425` that has since moved with the file. The tier's size is not this document's to state — `.github/ci-baselines/test-count-baseline.json` is the authority, and it records the web tier at 117 test files with 3125 cases executed. What is worth keeping is the mechanism: a latent timing flake that v8 instrumentation makes more likely is not a defect a coverage measurement introduced, so a red coverage run with a single timed-out `getByRole` is diagnosed here rather than re-discovered.
establishmentProvenance: HOSTED. Node 22 on ubuntu-latest, @vitest/coverage-v8 4.1.11, run id 34321869051. This field previously read LOCAL, PENDING A HOSTED RE-MEASUREMENT and pinned @vitest/coverage-v8 3.2.7; the hosted run named in `establishedBy` is the measurement that discharges it. The rule that field stated is the rule that was applied: where a hosted figure and a local one disagree, the hosted figure is the authority and this document is corrected in a commit that says so. For the record, the local run on the machine that prepared this commit (Node v24.19.0 on win32) reproduces the hosted raw counts on this tier exactly — 1875/2246, 2064/2517, 577/667, 1698/2153 across the same 131 files — so the two platforms do not disagree here at all.
measurementConventionNote: The percentages above are coverage-gate.mjs's own `pct()` — covered/total to two decimals, rounded — because that is what the ratchet compares against. The v8 text summary TRUNCATES instead. The worked example has been rebuilt on the current counts, because the old one (392/451) is a count this tier no longer holds. Functions are 577/667 = 86.5067…, printed as 86.50 by the truncating text summary and computed as 86.51 by the gate; `measuredAtEstablishment.functions` above records the truncated spelling 86.50, which is the conservative one. Branches are 1698/2153 = 78.8666…, printed as 78.86 and computed as 78.87. Both numbers are correct about different conventions; the gate's is authoritative here because the gate is what enforces. This is the same discrepancy coverage-baseline.backend.json records for its own tier, and it is written down again rather than left for the next reader to rediscover as a defect.
globalNote: Every floor sits BELOW its own measurement, deliberately. A floor recorded AT the run that produced it is a transcript, not a guard: the very next commit moves it, and the gate can only ever report what already happened. The headroom convention is unchanged across the re-establishment — 1.00 pp on lines and statements, 1.50 pp on functions and branches — and only the measurement it is subtracted from has moved: 83.48 -> 82.48 lines, 82.00 -> 81.00 statements, 86.50 -> 85.00 functions, 78.87 -> 77.37 branches. Functions and branches get more because they are coarse: 667 functions means one function is 0.15 pp, so a 1.00 pp band is under seven functions of churn, while 1.00 pp of lines is 22 lines of a 2,246-line denominator. Note the denominators themselves: they are roughly a fifth of the vitest-3 ones (2,246 lines against 11,145) because AST-aware remapping counts executable units rather than source ranges, which is why no percentage here can be read against the superseded one. Retaining the convention rather than pinning the floors at the measurement is what keeps `apps/web/tests/security.test.ts` — which requires 1 to 3 pp of headroom on every metric — a real assertion after the re-basing.
whatTheHeadroomGuarantees: With the 0.5 pp tolerance on top, and recomputed against the new denominators rather than carried over, the gate trips on: a net loss of more than 33 covered LINES, more than 37 covered STATEMENTS, more than 13 covered FUNCTIONS, or more than 43 covered BRANCHES, at a constant denominator. Those are the bounds the numbers actually enforce, stated as bounds rather than as a slogan about deleting a file. They are tighter in absolute terms than the superseded bounds (167 lines, 9 functions, 36 branches) purely because the denominators shrank; a smaller unit of account makes each covered unit worth more.
denominatorTrapNote: KNOWN TRAP, recorded because this project has already been bitten by it: a coverage percentage can FALL because v8 newly ENTERS code that was previously never loaded, so the module joins the denominator carrying its uncovered lines with it. This note used to say `coverage.all` is true in apps/web/vitest.config.ts. IT IS NOT, AND THE OPTION NO LONGER EXISTS — vitest 4 removed `coverage.all` and moved the guarantee to `coverage.include`: on a full-tier run the provider adds every file matching `include` that no test loaded, at zero, before the report is written. So the guarantee did not weaken, it moved, and what must never be narrowed is now the include list. `apps/web/tests/security.test.ts` pins that list; the repository-root and backend include lists are pinned the same way in `tests/ci/baseline-integrity.test.ts`. If a metric still falls, cover the code. Never lower these numbers to make a run pass, and never raise them from a local measurement.
touchedFileNote: The exemption is for the ROUTE tier only, and it is temporary rather than principled. `apps/web/src/app/[locale]/(dashboard)/**` is at 52.91% line coverage (354/669 across 55 files) — async React Server Components that no test currently renders. The figure this note used to carry, 7.62% (162/2125 across 26 files), is a vitest-3 measurement of a smaller tree and is not comparable: the file count grew with the router, and AST-aware remapping cut the denominator from 2125 to 669 by counting executable units instead of source ranges, which lifts the percentage without a line of these pages being newly exercised. The exemption still has a basis, because 52.91% is still under the 60% touched-file floor and a floor over these files would refuse every pull request that edits a page, for a gap this document RECORDS rather than fixes. It is NOT a claim that a route cannot be unit-tested; those files are deliberately still inside the measurement (see the exclusion comment in apps/web/vitest.config.ts). Remove this prefix once the route tier is covered.

knownGaps.supersededMeasurement: 7.62% — 162/2125 lines across 26 files, under @vitest/coverage-v8 3.2.7. Recorded so the jump is not read as coverage work: nothing in this branch renders a page that was not rendered before.
knownGaps.why: Async React Server Components. Nothing in the unit tier renders them, so the permission branch, the notFound() guard and the failed-catalogue fallback in each page are exercised only by the browser tier — which is a different tier with a different failure mode. No critical-module floor is set here on purpose: a floor at 52.91% would ratify the gap by writing it into the enforcement layer, and it would be a floor built on a number that is high for a measurement reason rather than a testing one.
knownGaps.closedBy: rendering the page functions in the dom project, or moving their decision logic into a covered module

knownGaps.supersededMeasurement: 0 and 0 — 0/31 and 0/40 lines under @vitest/coverage-v8 3.2.7, under the id `zero-coverage-library-modules`. The id was renamed because it no longer describes the files.
knownGaps.why: Two library modules that still carry no test of their own. Their reported coverage is NOT the result of tests being added: under AST-aware remapping the executable-unit denominators fall to 9 and 19, and the units that other modules' tests reach through them are now attributed as covered. The honest reading is that the previous 0% overstated the gap and the present 66.66/94.73 understates it; neither is a substitute for a direct test. Recorded rather than excluded. Note the consequence, which is unchanged: these files are NOT under the touched-file exemption, so a pull request that edits `format.ts` is still refused by the 60% touched-file floor until it carries a test. That is the gate working, not a fault to pre-empt.

criticalModules.why: the customer create, profile, governance and duplicate-review screens and the server actions behind them; P1-27 shipped ten canonical writes with a route, a permission and no screen anybody could reach them from, and this is the code that closed that
VIN entry, duplicate review, documents, history and relations — the surface where a silent wrong write was found by hand while every automated tier was green
every request the browser makes, plus the idempotency table, the read-operation outcome classification and the session cookie; a defect here is wrong for all screens at once
decides which control a reader is shown; WRITE_PERMISSIONS once had zero consumers while ten write forms rendered for anybody
the one module that assembles the CSP; an unsafe-eval or a wildcard source here is the difference between stopping an injected script and not
maps a 422 onto the field that caused it; when this is wrong an operator is told nothing is wrong and the record is not saved
scores and explains a candidate match; an over-confident score merges two customers and P1-OD-017 keeps the merge caller shut precisely because of it
the shared directory contract every CRM read goes through; a keyset cursor defect here drops rows silently, which this repository has already shipped once

criticalModulesNote: Every floor sits below its own recorded measurement. The margins are no longer the uniform 5-7 points this note used to claim, because `measuredAtEstablishment` on each rule has been REFRESHED to the vitest-4 hosted run named in `establishedBy` while NO FLOOR MOVED: `crm-customer-surface` 94.31 over 92, `vehicle-surface` 97.12 over 91, `api-client` 98.51 over 92, `client-permissions` 100 over 95, `content-security-policy` 100 over 95, `form-results-and-field-errors` 95.24 over 90, `duplicate-scoring` 95.65 over 90, `customer-directory` 96.55 over 90. All eight pass. The margin now runs from 2.31 points on `crm-customer-surface` to 6.51 on `api-client`, and the narrow one is the one to watch: `tolerancePercentagePoints` does NOT apply to a critical module — coverage-gate.mjs compares a module measurement against its floor directly — so 2.31 points of a 422-line denominator is about ten lines of CRM churn. That is stated as where the tier stands, NOT as a case for lowering 92. `minMatchedFiles` pins how many instrumented files each prefix currently governs: a coverage `include` list narrows SILENTLY, so without this, removing files shrinks what the floor protects while the percentage stays reassuring. It is a MINIMUM, not an equality — `customer-directory` now matches 4 instrumented files against its declared 2, recorded on that rule as `matchedFilesAtReEstablishment`, because the matched set widened as the directory grew rather than because the rule changed; the pin is left at 2 so this pass moves no threshold in either direction. coverage-gate.mjs additionally refuses any rule whose prefix matches nothing, so a renamed directory turns the gate red instead of turning the rule off.
